first_impression.reaction: Googled 'wedding ceremony script australia' on the train. Good: the first paragraph is literally the answer, the words the celebrant has to say, in quote marks. No pop-up, no 'your big day is a magical journey' waffle. The very first sentence is a mouthful on a phone though, I had to read it twice to find where the actual quote starts. Key takeaways are right there under it, which is what I read next. I'd scroll straight to the script, copy it, and bookmark the page.

journey.quote: In Australia, a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination must say the monitum in section 46(1) of the Marriage Act 1961, which opens "I am duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages according to law", or words to that effect, before you are married.
journey.reaction: This is the answer, so tick. But it's one long sentence with three qualifiers before I get to the quote. Split it and it'd land in five seconds instead of fifteen.

journey.quote: Everything else is yours. This guide sets those words inside a full, original wedding ceremony script Australia's celebrants can work from, with every part marked legally required or optional.
journey.reaction: 'Everything else is yours' is a nice line. And 'marked legally required or optional' tells me exactly why this page is different from the US scripts I usually get.

journey.quote: An authorised celebrant must be physically present with the two of you and 2 witnesses over 18, and all of you sign 3 marriage certificates on the day.
journey.reaction: Specific numbers, no fluff. That's the kind of thing I'd screenshot. The takeaways don't tell me the full script is further down though, I had to scroll to find out.

journey.quote: General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Answers my 'is this still true in 2026?' straight away, so good the first time. By the sixth time I've seen the same line it's just noise on a small screen.
Quoted with the section number and a link to the actual legislation. That's why I'd trust this over a random blog.

journey.section: The Australian wedding ceremony script, word for word
journey.quote: **Legally required** for a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination, unless they hold a section 46(2) exemption.
journey.reaction: The bold Legally required / Optional labels make this really easy to scan. This is the bit I came for. The monitum is printed in full here and again higher up, which is a lot of scrolling, but I get that the script needs to be complete to copy.

journey.quote: Legal vow, first partner, to the second: "I call upon the persons here present to witness that I, [full name], take thee, [full name], to be my lawful wedded [wife, husband or spouse]."
journey.reaction: Clear. My first thought is 'do we really have to say thee?'. The page says 'or words to that effect' and to ask the celebrant, which is fair, but I still don't know if 'you' is fine.

journey.quote: For a small legal ceremony before a larger celebration, this is the core with nothing added.
journey.reaction: Love this. Four numbered steps. If I'm doing a quick registry-style thing before the real party, this is all I need.

journey.quote: If this ceremony is one moment in a longer weekend, with guests flying in and a venue to secure, Wedded Concierge plans the whole celebration around it.
journey.reaction: First time I see the brand and I don't know what Wedded Concierge is yet. It's one line and doesn't block anything, so I just scroll past.

journey.section: Marrying overseas or holding a symbolic ceremony
journey.quote: If you are overseas now, you can complete the notice of intended marriage from abroad when you plan to marry in Australia.
journey.reaction: Useful for me sitting in Singapore. Answers a next question I didn't know I had.

journey.quote: It is the statement in section 46(1) of the Marriage Act 1961 that a civil celebrant says to you, in front of your witnesses, before you marry.
journey.reaction: If I jumped straight to the FAQ, this answer tells me what a monitum is legally but not what it actually says or is for. Feels thin next to the others.

unanswered_questions: Can we say 'you' instead of 'thee' in the legal vow, or is that something only the celebrant can decide?
Can the witnesses be family members, like a parent or sibling?
Is there a printable or downloadable copy of the full script?
What exactly is Wedded Concierge and is it only for weddings abroad? The page never says in one plain line.

cta_reaction.quote: When the ceremony is set, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: I came for a script, not a planner. The CTAs are polite and don't get in the way, which I appreciate, and I might click the magazine link later for ideas. But nothing here makes me want to talk to someone today. 'Works in your time zone' is a nice touch for someone overseas.

top_3_changes: Split the opening sentence so the quote lands faster on a phone. OLD: "In Australia, a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination must say the monitum in section 46(1) of the Marriage Act 1961, which opens "I am duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages according to law", or words to that effect, before you are married." NEW: "In Australia, a civil celebrant (one who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination) must say the monitum in section 46(1) of the Marriage Act 1961, or words to that effect, before you are married. It opens "I am duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages according to law"." (keep the fact_18 comment after it).

Tell the skimmer the full script is on the page, in Key takeaways. OLD: "- An Australian celebrant cannot perform a legal marriage overseas, so a celebration abroad pairs with a legal ceremony at home or follows the destination's own law." NEW: "- An Australian celebrant cannot perform a legal marriage overseas, so a celebration abroad pairs with a legal ceremony at home or follows the destination's own law.
- The full script below marks every part legally required or optional, followed by a four-step short legal script."

Make the FAQ monitum answer stand on its own. OLD: "It is the statement in section 46(1) of the Marriage Act 1961 that a civil celebrant says to you, in front of your witnesses, before you marry." NEW: "It is the statement in section 46(1) of the Marriage Act 1961 that a civil celebrant says to you, in front of your witnesses, before you marry. It reminds you of the solemn and binding nature of marriage, and the full wording is quoted in the script above." (keep the fact_18 comment after it).
